title: The Prophet
text: It was some time after that whole incident that Father was summoned to the Four Heroes Church in Faubrey, ostensibly for an inspection, so I tagged along to pay a visit myself, I say. The Four Heroes Church in Faubrey, having suffered tremendous damage from the whole Takt affair, was in the middle of restoration work. Apparently all sorts of historically significant relics had been smashed to pieces in the chaos of the war.
“Motoyasu, you came here safe and sound during your loop, right?”
“Indeed I did.”

Ah, how nostalgic. It brought back memories of coming here with Father and the others on our way to Faubrey. During that particular loop, I’d visited this church several times and seen and heard all sorts of things.
“If you remember it, that’s convenient. Help with the restoration work, as much as your memory allows.”
“Leave it to me, I say.”
Takt’s scars ran deep, and the damage to the Four Heroes Church remained vivid and raw. The inscriptions meant to be shown to the Heroes had, for the most part, taken heavy damage and been shattered.
“Heh… so this is the place where all the belongings left behind by the holders of the sacred weapons throughout the generations used to be, huh.”
“Relics born of faith. You find that sort of thing in quite a lot of worlds, don’t you.”
“Yeah.”
And so, Ark and Hou-kun had come along with us as well.
“Hou, didn’t you say you know how to read the writing the Heroes left behind? Can you reproduce it?”
“You need it restored? Well, if I take a look, I think I can piece it back together to some extent.”
“That goddess smashed everything she could get her hands on. Restoring it would make for a fine bit of spite, wouldn’t it? And it’d serve as a lesson for later generations too.”
“Wow… so it doubles as spite too. Never thought of using restoration that way—how novel.”
“It’s important to lay down some defenses so it doesn’t all go to waste. Well then, let’s get to work.”

And so, in that manner, we all pitched in to help restore the inscriptions the Heroes had left behind in the Four Heroes Church. Specifically, it was a matter of fitting the shattered pieces of the inscriptions back together like a jigsaw puzzle. It required at least some ability to read the text, but it seemed the power that let letters glow and surface in my memory had faded away, I say.
“Huh… so this is the prophecy inscription.”
“I see, I see.”
Ark and Hou-kun each muttered to themselves as they looked over the inscription mid-restoration.
“A prophecy, huh… now that I think about it, apparently the story of how we ended up summoned to this world was told through this. Whoever left this behind—what kind of person were they, I wonder.”
“Aren’t you going to check?”
“I want to, but…”
“Well, even if you tried, you couldn’t. She’s good at erasing her traces. Unless you already have some idea who she is, you wouldn’t even notice her at all,” Ark answered.
“You know her? Or rather, was this inscription carved while you were still around?”
“Hmm? No, this was made after I left. Ah… honestly, it really does seem like she scattered these all over the world after I disappeared.”
Oh? So it seemed Ark had an acquaintance involved here. Could this be the one who wrote the inscription, I wondered?
“Is it you, Hou-kun?”
“This is my first time coming to this world. So no, it’s not me.”
“Was it Cal Mira Island? There was one written on a stone monument there too. And apparently, she didn’t even let the mastermind who ravaged this world realize her true identity.”
“Just who the hell is this person. Some kind of god-hunter who just lets that bastard’s misdeeds slide?”

“Hmm… well, she’s chosen to remain a bystander now, so… but yeah, I’d say she was setting up all sorts of things behind the scenes so you all could overcome your trials. She lent a hand from the shadows.”
“How irresponsible.”

Father looked utterly exasperated. Well, of course. A god-hunter who just lets the Crimson Swine run wild with her mischief sounds like quite the scoundrel, I say. But going by what Ark and the others were saying, it seemed this might be the very person who’d left magic inscriptions scattered across the frontier settlements.
“I’d rather you not put it that way. She’s practically a ghost of her former self by now… but I get it, I understand the reasoning.”
“Well, that’s true. That girl’s got an outrageous knack for foreseeing the future.”
“The Lucor fruit exists in this world, so it wouldn’t be strange for her to stop by. It’s a fruit tied to memories, after all.”
“Hm? Wait, that means…”
Father and Big Sister furrowed their brows and tilted their heads, and at that, Ark and Hou-kun nodded.

“Yeah. The demon girl we talked about regarding the Lucor fruit incident. Years after she sealed me away… originally she was already a strong kid, but that overwhelming power of hers ran out of control, and in the process she ended up gaining the power of foresight.”
“It was pretty intense, from what I heard. Seeing too much apparently caused her a lot of trouble. Catching her would be difficult, I’d think.”
“I figured it was unrelated so I let it slide, but has that person been to this world too?”
This, apparently, was the one who’d fallen mutually in love with the subordinate born of Ark’s anger. The one said to have left behind the prophecy that led to our summoning, I say.
“So it wasn’t the Crimson Swine who left it behind to push forward the Hero Summoning ritual, then?”
“There’s a chance someone imitated her and left similar things behind, but this one was undoubtedly left by her.”
“I’d guess… she probably left it around the time she was summoned as something like the Claw Hero. When it comes to spirit vessels—sacred weapons—no one surpasses her.”
“Why’s that?”

“Why, you ask… ah, I guess I never explained. She was the very first to create what came to be called the sacred weapons. The original prototype was a device meant to let anyone use techniques that were originally hers alone, but then spirits took up residence within it, and it became a vessel for spirits.”

Oh ho… so Ark and Hou-kun knew exactly how the sacred weapons had come to be. Now that I thought of it, I recalled Ark disassembling and reassembling something that looked like a sacred weapon late one night—was that not it, I wondered?
“The spirits apparently have a hard time finding her too, so they gather around me instead, since I carry a kind of marker.”

Ark muttered this with a sigh, and at that, a light that looked like a spirit appeared and began bobbing up and down in agreement. It seemed Ark couldn’t actually see it, because he noticed the rest of us tracking the light with our eyes and tilted his head in confusion.
“Something like a spirit was bobbing up and down just now,” Naofumi said.
“Is that so? I can’t see it at all.”
“Not being able to see it is a real pain, honestly. Spare a thought for the poor interpreter, would you,” Hou-kun grumbled.
I could relate. In my case, I always had various people translate pig-speech for me, I say.
“What kind of person is she, anyway?”

“These days she’s mostly in her demon form. In that form, she’s… a large cat-beastman, I’d say. Sometimes she manifests bat wings if she wants to. She’s technically a vampire too, come to think of it.”
Father looked over at Ark.
“Yeah. She dumped her overflowing power onto me out of spite and forced me into this form. At a glance, we look similar enough that we might pass for parent and child.”

“There are definitely times she pretends to be you and makes a run for it. She burrowed into you for a while too, and tore off a fragment of power before making her exit—she’s incredibly good at erasing her presence.”
“Probably,” Ark agreed.
It seemed the prophet in question bore a striking resemblance to Ark.
“The difference is her tail stays cat-shaped, and the size. Cats can shrink down small, but she stays big. Her build and coloring are a bit off too—if you called her a tiger, she’d get mad.”
“Sounds like just a big cat-beastman to me. Is she really mistakable for a tiger-beastman?”
“Right?! She doesn’t have a demi-human form, but she can turn into a human too.”
“Honestly, both that bird and her have saddled me with nothing but trouble. Because of it, reincarnators in this world have come after me too… well, I suppose I get targeted regardless.”

That… could it be referring to becoming immortal, I wondered? I recalled hearing from some pig or another that drinking a phoenix’s blood grants immortality. From the sound of it, it seemed both Hou-kun and this woman of his had similarly saddled Ark with the power of immortality. As Father and the others chatted amongst themselves, I kept piecing together the puzzle, intent on restoring the inscription—when suddenly, it gave off a faint glow. This was… surely something worth reporting—and just as that thought crossed my mind, the contents of the text left me utterly speechless.

You who make this text shine—I leave this for you, who have heard the chaos cat and the phoenix speaking of me. Should you report this now, the future you desire shall not come to pass. The one you believe in, the messenger from the heavens, and your happiness shall all draw nearer to ruin.
That was the sentence that first came into view.
